spacing.$description: Primitive spacing steps. Step 1 is the base multiplier (0.25rem); every other step is that multiplier times its own key, which is what Tailwind's spacing utilities compute. The fractional keys survive into CSS with the dot escaped.

font.$description: Typeface stacks. The sans stack names the interface face the component package ships, then the metric-adjusted fallback it ships beside it, then the platform stack; the mono stack is fixed-width and this package ships nothing for it, so every entry is one the reader's own machine provides.

font-weight.$description: Numeric weights matching the Inter faces the component package ships, which are the three the scale renders at plus the one italic. `normal` is named to match the utility it generates rather than `regular`.

text.$description: Type scale. Each step carries its own line-height in $extensions so the emitted `--text-*--line-height` companion is authored here, not left to Tailwind's default. Every step is a whole multiple of 0.125rem, and the gaps at the top of the group are the widest it authors: `4xl` to `5xl` is four thirds and `5xl` to `6xl` is five fourths, where the gaps below it are one fifth to one quarter. The two largest steps are the display role, they are the ceiling of the whole system, and `SectionHeading`'s level table is what reaches them.

leading.$description: Unitless line-heights. Use these with the text scale where a step's own line-height is not the one wanted.

tracking.$description: Letter-spacing steps, in em so they scale with the type size.

duration.$description: Motion durations. Pair with the easing tokens below; never hardcode a duration in a component.

ease.$description: Easing curves. `out` is the default for state feedback; `in-out` is for a state that moves both ways. No control point overshoots.

ambient.$description: Ambient cycle lengths for a figure that shows a system running. These are deliberately two orders of magnitude longer than `duration`, because they measure a cycle rather than a state change: a packet crossing a rail, a wavefront crossing a field, a scan crossing a chart. A component names one of these and one of the `ambient-ease` curves below, and never a second or a `cubic-bezier(...)` literal. There is no 'loop' keyframe here: the keyframes live in the component package's own stylesheet, because a keyframe is a mechanism and a duration is a value.

ambient-ease.$description: Easing for an ambient cycle, separated from `ease` because the two answer different questions. `ease` shapes a response to something a reader did; these shape a loop nobody triggered, and a loop that eases in and out on every cycle reads as a machine stuttering rather than as one running. `linear` is for anything that carries a thing from one place to another, because a marker that accelerates and decelerates is a marker being served rather than a marker travelling. As in `ease`, no control point y exceeds 1, so nothing here overshoots.
